data.name: RescueStock
data.idea: Emergency purchasing assistant for small cafés: Arabic/English request and optional package image to structured requirements, exact supply plans over indivisible cup/lid bundles from demonstration suppliers, buyer approval, atomic inventory reservation, supplier confirmation, PayPal Sandbox authorize-then-capture per supplier with compensation, replanning when a supplier drops out. PayPal AI Hackathon entry built with ECCode 0.3.0.

data.title: Workflow level
data.rationale: Payments (PayPal authorize/capture/void/refund), authentication, inventory invariants and AI extraction change trust boundaries; orchestrate skill section 1 routes such work to the full delivery with the security reviewer on the phases that touch the boundary.

data.notes: Brief restating RS-REQ-1 verbatim (RS-01..33, RS-NF-1..4 as NFR1-4), additions RS-34..39, NFR5-6

data.title: PayPal Sandbox hosts blocked from the build environment; live PayPal evidence cannot be produced here
data.mitigation: Fake adapter implements the full provider contract with fault injection; live Sandbox suite scripted with a runbook for the user's machine; evidence table marks live rows Unverified with the exact blocker

data.title: No PayPal credentials and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY in the build environment
data.mitigation: Credentials only via env (NFR4); Claude Code CLI is the working real-model route; user asked for Sandbox credentials (Q1) and model route/spend (Q3)

data.title: Double capture under repeated clicks, retries or lost responses
data.mitigation: Unique operation key per payment operation, PayPal-Request-Id = operation key, intent persisted before every external call, state machine forbids capture from captured/unknown, reconciler fetches provider state before any retry; RS-20 and RS-25 tests

data.title: Double reservation / oversell under concurrent customers
data.mitigation: Conditional UPDATE (reserved + qty <= on_hand) inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, CHECK constraints, unique operation_key, release-once ledger; RS-14/15/16 multi-process tests on a real SQLite file

data.title: Cross-account access between customers, suppliers and admin tools
data.mitigation: RBAC default-deny, owner-scoped queries in the service layer, admin routes role-gated; RS-27/28/30 tests; independent security review

data.title: Prompt injection via image or catalog text alters extraction or downstream behaviour
data.mitigation: Model output schema-validated and treated as data; model has no tools; permissions, amounts, suppliers and plan versions never derived from model output; buyer confirms fields; RS-05 injection fixtures

data.title: Model unavailability, latency or cost blow-up
data.mitigation: Deterministic fake provider for tests; haiku default; timeouts; per-run cost ceiling recorded per extraction (NFR6)

data.title: Lost or unknown payment outcome leaves money or stock in limbo
data.mitigation: unknown operation state, reconciler fetches provider state, reservation reconciling is never auto-released, escalation flag on failed compensation; RS-22/25/26

data.title: PayPal secrets leak into frontend assets, logs, screenshots or submission materials
data.mitigation: Config redaction, hosted approval link keeps client id off the browser, automated secret scan test (RS-29), .env.example placeholders only

data.title: Hackathon facts unverified against the official Devpost page (deadline, rules, judging)
data.mitigation: User re-checks the official page (Q5); schedule keeps margin before the reported 12 Nov 2026 deadline

data.title: Scope breadth versus time budget (33 mandatory tests, three dashboards, live suites)
data.mitigation: Slices S1-S8 ordered by risk; fake adapters complete the deterministic suite early; minimal state-driven frontend; verification gate records any unverified row honestly

data.title: Sandbox webhooks unreachable in the demo (no public URL)
data.mitigation: Signature verification path tested with the fake adapter and recorded Sandbox payloads; polling fallback for provider order state (A10, Q6)

handoff.objective: Produce and submit the RescueStock architecture brief (users, problem, requirements, workflows, acceptance criteria, scope, architecture, constraints, success criteria, assumptions, open questions, risk register) for independent review at the architecture gate.
handoff.context: Inputs are the user's master goal (docs/build/goal.md, requirements version RS-REQ-1: RS-01..RS-33, RS-NF-1..4, fixture RS-FIX-1, assumptions A1-A5, unverified hackathon facts) and the architecture draft (docs/build/plan.md: zero-dependency Node 22 + node:sqlite stack, modules, data model, contracts, exact planner with oracle, payment saga). Environment facts verified in this session: api-m.sandbox.paypal.com and developer.paypal.com are blocked by network policy; no PayPal credentials and no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; Claude Code CLI (claude -p --json-schema, haiku/sonnet, billed to the user) works as the real-model route; Playwright + Chromium installed; Node 22.22; node:sqlite available; PostgreSQL not running. eccode memory search returned no records, so no lessons were cited.
handoff.expectedOutput: .eccode/artifacts/architecture/brief.md submitted to the architecture gate with one acceptance criterion per user requirement id, risks recorded with eccode risk add, and this handoff.
acceptanceCriteria: Brief contains every gate-checked heading (Users, Problem, Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, Architecture, Assumptions, Open Questions, Risks) plus Main Workflows, Scope, Constraints, Success Criteria

Every user requirement id RS-01..RS-33 appears verbatim as an acceptance-criterion id; RS-NF-1..4 appear as NFR1..NFR4 with the user id in parentheses (the gate's id grammar allows one hyphen); no requirement weakened, renumbered or dropped
eccode gate show architecture lists RS-01..RS-39 and NFR1..NFR6 as required criteria
Material risks recorded as RISK-1..RISK-12 with honest severities and named mitigations
Open questions that need the user are listed with the decision each blocks
handoff.completedWork: Wrote brief.md restating the goal and plan densely without weakening any RS id. Added RS-34..RS-39 (simulation labelling, six on-screen questions, separate state machines with derived rescue status, guarded admin reset, append-only ledgers, image upload limits) and NFR5 (performance) and NFR6 (cost/observability), all derived from the goal's prose. Architecture adopts plan.md sections 2-6 unchanged, adds a text diagram, trust boundaries, and justifies each major choice against an alternative (SQLite vs PostgreSQL, exact planner vs greedy, hosted approval link vs JS SDK, credential-per-merchant vs partner API, CLI vs API model route, stateful fake adapter vs HTTP mocks, single process vs services). Added the AI feature statement (failure modes, human-in-the-loop points, quality thresholds). Submitted as sub-mv15wpmr-015f7530; eccode gate show confirms 45 required criteria (RS-01..RS-39, NFR1..NFR6). Recorded RISK-1..RISK-12 (RISK-3 double capture, RISK-4 double reservation, RISK-5 cross-account access are critical; RISK-1 blocked Sandbox hosts and RISK-2 missing credentials are high). Decision: the four RS-NF ids are listed as NFR1-4 (RS-NF-x) because the parser rejects a second hyphen; the user id is preserved in the item text and in the Requirements section.
remainingIssues: Q1: number of PayPal Sandbox business accounts/REST credentials (one per supplier A-E or one shared) - blocks A2 wiring and live RS-18..RS-26
Q2: where the live PayPal suite runs (user's machine with network) - blocks live evidence for NFR3
Q3: model route and spend ceiling (CLI haiku/sonnet or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) - blocks NFR6 ceiling and live RS-01..03
Q4: dedicated public repository vs examples/rescuestock in ECCode - blocks README paths and submission links
Q5: user to confirm deadline, submission requirements and judging on the official Devpost page (blocked here)
Q6: public webhook URL for Sandbox webhooks or polling fallback acceptable - blocks live RS-23/24 design
Q7: Devpost account/project ownership and demo video production (Devpost connector needs interactive authorization)
Q8: English-only interface acceptable for Arabic-speaking buyers (no RTL planned) - blocks NFR2 scope
Live PayPal Sandbox evidence cannot be produced in this environment (RISK-1, RISK-2); the fake adapter covers the paths deterministically
handoff.nextAction: architecture-reviewer reviews submission sub-mv15wpmr-015f7530 against all 45 required criteria; the orchestrator relays Q1-Q8 to the user; on changes_requested, product-architect revises brief.md and resubmits with --responds-to.
